name: Medical tourism in Kerala
tagline: Advanced hospitals, Ayurveda and seamless patient services in a tropical setting
summary: Kerala combines internationally accredited hospitals and world-class Ayurveda and wellness centres, supported by government promotion and patient‑support services for international visitors.
description: Medical tourism in Kerala covers high‑end allopathic care (cardiac, oncology, orthopaedics, transplants and robotic surgery) alongside traditional Ayurveda and wellness programmes — all supported by a growing network of international‑patient services.

The state promotes medical value travel through the Kerala Medical Value Travel Society (KMVTS) and government tourism initiatives; private hospitals increasingly hold NABH/NABL or international accreditations and hospitals pair clinical treatment with recovery stays in coastal or hill destinations.

Visitors find cost advantages, short wait times for many procedures, and a recovery environment with easy access to Ayurveda, physiotherapy and rehabilitation. Always confirm treatment plans, cost estimates and visa requirements with your chosen provider before travel.
highlights: Strong Ayurveda & wellness sector alongside tertiary care hospitals
Many hospitals hold NABH / NABL (and some JCI) accreditation
State medical value travel portal (KMVTS) lists hospitals and patient services
Eased e‑visa/medical‑visa processes and government promotion since 2024–2026
Good connectivity via Kochi, Thiruvananthapuram and Kozhikode airports

sections.heading: Background
body: Kerala’s medical tourism mixes modern tertiary hospitals with traditional Indian systems of medicine (Ayurveda). The state government and industry created the Kerala Medical Value Travel Society (KMVTS) to market services and provide a single information portal for hospitals, doctors and travel guidance.

National data show medical‑purpose foreign tourist arrivals remain a material segment of India’s inbound travel; Kerala’s industry emphasises both clinical care (surgery, oncology, cardiology, transplants) and longer wellness stays for Panchakarma and rehabilitation.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Choose accredited hospitals for complex procedures — many major centres in Kochi and Thiruvananthapuram offer international patient departments, multidisciplinary teams and advanced tech such as robotic surgery and 3D planning.

For wellness and recovery, book accredited Ayurveda resorts or ISM (Indian System of Medicine) hospitals for structured therapies, Panchakarma packages and post‑operative rehabilitation; combine clinical appointments with gentle destination recovery (backwaters, beaches, hill stations).

Ask hospitals for an international patient coordinator, written cost estimates, treatment timelines and required pre‑travel tests. Verify whether your insurer covers repatriation and post‑op complications.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Start by using KMVTS or the hospital’s international‑patient office to shortlist accredited providers, request consultation notes, and get a formal appointment and estimate. Pre‑validation of the Medical/Ayush visa is required — hospitals can generate the invitation/validation letter through the Medical & Ayush Visa portal.

Arrange travel to Kochi (Cochin International Airport – COK), Thiruvananthapuram (TRV) or Kozhikode (CCJ) depending on your hospital, and plan 2–4 weeks extra for recovery if you combine surgery with rehabilitation or Ayurveda. Confirm availability and fees before booking travel and accommodation.

latest.text: PIB published national figures for foreign tourist arrivals for medical purposes and confirmed India’s e‑medical visa facilities continue to support medical travel.
Industry commentary highlights rapid adoption of advanced medical technologies in Kerala (robotic surgery, 3D planning) and estimates substantial annual international patient volumes.

Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) figures reported by press: ayurvedic medical value tourism in Kerala generated INR 13,500 crore in 2024 and foreign arrivals for therapeutic services rose in 2024.
Kerala Medical Value Travel Society (KMVTS) launches a public web portal listing hospitals, doctors, travel guides and medical‑visa procedures to promote the state’s medical value travel offer.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Year‑round; October–March is popular for recovery and Ayurveda stays (post‑monsoon, cooler weather).
visitorInfo.howToReach: Fly to Kochi (COK), Thiruvananthapuram (TRV) or Kozhikode (CCJ); major hospitals run airport pickup and international patient services. Domestic rail and road networks connect all health hubs.
etiquette: Use accredited hospitals (NABH/NABL/JCI) and ask for an international patient coordinator and a written cost estimate.
Get a pre‑validated Medical or Ayush visa invitation letter from your hospital via the Medical & Ayush Visa portal before applying.
Carry full medical records, medication lists and an English translation if needed; arrange travel insurance that covers overseas procedures and repatriation.
Confirm package inclusions (post‑op care, physiotherapy, Ayurveda sessions) and recovery‑time advice before booking tourist activities.
